hypothesis_update: Working hypothesis: actions declared `Internal` are filtered out of the kernel's action list (compose.rs:326-328), yet `SyncAction`s (compose.rs:354-356) are the invocation mechanism for them. If `sync_action` does not separately emit or re-include the referenced internal action's rewritten body, the lowered kernel will contain a sync action whose target is absent — a silent data-integrity/behavioral defect; if its lookup is strict over the filtered set, this instead surfaces as an unreachable 'unknown action' error. Secondary observation to verify while there: the merged single `SpecItem::Init` (compose.rs:360-364) concatenates all component inits (rewritten with an empty alias set) before compose-level inits, so I'm watching for an ordering/aliasing hazard, but the sync-vs-internal interaction is the primary uncertainty. Awaiting the sync_action body (sync-alias-boundary) to confirm which outcome holds and to see the arity-mismatch check.
rationale: The received target body shows a concrete interaction I cannot yet resolve: component actions marked `Internal` are excluded from `actions` (compose.rs:326-328 via `if !internal.contains(...)`), while `ComposeItem::SyncAction` entries push the result of `sync_action(action, &components, &mut warnings)` (compose.rs:354-356). The documented contract explicitly lists "unknown aliases or actions" and "sync arity mismatches" as error conditions, both of which must live inside `sync_action`. This is the single highest-uncertainty spot for a data-integrity defect: whether `sync_action` resolves its targets against the same action set that just dropped the internal actions (→ a sync action whose referenced internal action body was never emitted = dangling reference / silent dropped behavior), or whether it re-includes internal action bodies. Reading sync-alias-boundary directly confirms or refutes the hypothesis and also reveals the arity check.
